properties.areaDesc: Northeast Suffolk
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 7:40PM EST until November 27 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, 1 to 1 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Northeast Suffolk County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 4
PM EST Friday.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also
extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 4 to 8 ft will result in
areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave
splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is
potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina
structures as well.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to
provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest
winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level
forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday
morning, and if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be
lowered slightly. Similarly if strongest winds linger later
into the evening, the Thursday evening water level forecast
could be a few tenths higher.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 3, locally 3 1/2
ft, of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable
areas near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, up to 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of inundation above ground
level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline.

* WHERE...Southwest Suffolk County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major
flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront.
Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become
flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront
along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result
in widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of
high tide. There is potential for localized overwashes
resulting in some flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to
provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest
winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level
forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday
morning, and if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be
lowered slightly. Similarly if strongest winds linger later
into the evening, the Thursday evening water level forecast
could be a few tenths higher.

water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 4:35PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding with up to 2.5 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW)
at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,

surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.description:

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 800 PM EST.

* At 717 PM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from near Pacific
Reef to 19 nm east of Carysfort Reef Light to 34 nm northeast of
Floyd's Wall Northeast, moving northeast at 35 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
9 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Carteret, NC; Craven, NC; Jones, NC; Onslow, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 6:18PM EST until November 25 at 9:15PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Carteret County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Craven County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Jones County in eastern North Carolina...
Onslow County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 618 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Jacksonville, Havelock, Morehead City, Newport, Harkers Island,
Piney Green, Camp Lejeune Center, Pumpkin Center, New River
Station, Stella, Swansboro, Hubert, Cape Carteret, North River,
Straits, Smyrna, Marshallberg, Pine Knoll Shores, Harlowe and
Silverdale.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: The Coastal Flood Watch has been replaced. Please see the latest information from NWS Eureka CA on this developing situation.
properties.description: The Coastal Flood Watch has been replaced. Please see the latest information from NWS Eureka CA on this developing situation.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 3:14PM PST until November 25 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves large
breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may worsen coastal flooding
along exposed beaches.. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater inundation above
ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways.
Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is
predicted.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM PST this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday.
High tide is at 12:54 PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide
gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before
and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be
higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.

properties.description:

for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Confidence has
increased for a slightly weaker system moving into the panhandle
during peak tides. Tides may exceed astronomical high tide, though
the likelihood of exceeding a foot has been reduced significantly.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 5:29PM EST until November 26 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A large portion of central North Carolina, including the
following counties: Alamance, Chatham, Cumberland, Durham,
Edgecombe, Forsyth, Franklin, Granville, Guilford, Halifax,
Harnett, Hoke, Johnston, Lee, Moore, Nash, Orange, Person,
Randolph, Sampson, Vance, Wake, Warren, Wayne and Wilson.

* WHEN...Through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A vigorous storm system with anomalous moisture and strong lift
will cause rain to expand and become moderate to heavy tonight
into Thursday morning. A broad area of 2 to 5 inches is expected,
with localized higher amounts between 5 and 8 inches possible in
the Coastal Plain and adjacent eastern Piedmont and Sandhills.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:24PM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides,
combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave
heights of 20 to 25 ft, will bring 2.5 to 3.0 ft of inundation
above ground level in low-lying areas and shorelines on
Thursday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities
of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos
Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway
101, especially around Coos Bay.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Roads may be closed. Low lying property including
homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be
inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the highest high tide early Thursday afternoon. Storm
activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be
present, which will likely maintain inundation impacts. At the
Charleston, Oregon tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at
12:23 PM Thursday. Minor coastal flooding is also still possible
on Friday with the high tide at 1:14 PM. Tides look to return
to more typical heights over the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:17PM PST until November 27 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops, will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this evening to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow
morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning.
Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding
flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM PST.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Thursday to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 7.8 feet will peak
between 9 AM and 11 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:08PM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, through 1 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, through 4 AM PST Friday. Most
susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the
morning high tide, around 9 AM on Thursday and 10 PM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides on Thursday will be around 8
feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-6
feet today. A long period west swell arrives late this
afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by Thursday
morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with
local sets up to 10-12 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers
to 3-6 feet by Friday morning's high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in the District of Columbia, Arlington
County, and the City of Alexandria.

* WHEN...From 3 PM Thursday to 3 AM EST Friday, especially
around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding is expected at the DC seafood market and in
portions of East Potomac Park. Water is expected to cover the
boardwalk at Washington Harbour. An increasing number of
streets and parks are flooded in Alexandria. Access to
Daingerfield Island is cut off.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides up to 4 feet above normal. The next
high tide at Alexandria is at 8:27 PM and 9:06 AM. The next high
tide at Washington Channel is at 8:09 PM and 8:48 AM.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Dauphin
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 4:17PM EST until November 26 at 10:00PM EST by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Dauphin County.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 10 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will blow from east to west, which could
put additional stress on trees and powerlines. The strongest wind
gusts are expected Thursday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Do not touch downed lines and report any power outages to your
electric company. Travel is highly discouraged due to slick roadways
and the possibility of downed trees and power lines.

Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location prior to
the onset of winds.

properties.headline: Gale Warning issued November 25 at 1:15PM PST until November 26 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, seas 16 to 21 ft at 16 seconds
and south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 45 kt. For the
Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous seas 13 to 17
ft at 13 seconds and southwest winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up
to 30 kt expected.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Cape Foulweather to Florence OR
out 10 NM and Waters from Cape Foulweather to Florence OR from
10 to 60 NM.

* WHEN...Gale Warning, until 10 AM PST Thursday. Hazardous Seas
Warning, from 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Central Coast of Oregon
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 12:28PM PST until November 26 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected
for beaches and headlands.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 7 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines. Some
power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult for high
profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The period of strongest winds are expected to
occur between 3-7 AM PST Thursday. Although it will be windy for
inland coastal communities, maximum gusts will be relatively weaker
compared to beaches and headlands with gusts up to 50-55 mph.
properties.instruction:
A High Wind Warning for the coastal headlands and beaches means a
hazardous high wind event is expected or occurring in those areas
along the immediate coast. Many of the headland areas and beaches are
vulnerable to very strong wind gusts that may pose a safety hazard
for individuals or high profile vehicles. The strong winds may also
cause property and/or tree damage. Sustained wind speeds of at least
40 mph or gusts of 58 mph or more are expected in those areas.
Coastal headlands are characterized by high, rocky shores and steep
sea cliffs.

Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 2:49PM EST until November 26 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:32PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels on
the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood Stage.
The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest this
weekend, reaching 6.4 feet, where it is expected to linger into early
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river is forecast to rise above the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 5.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.4 feet Saturday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:24PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage, above its
previous record flood stage. River levels are forecast to hold near a
crest of 13.2 to 13.3 feet through late week, before beginning a very
slow decline within Major flood stage this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 13.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.3 feet
this evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:18PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise  through late week, reaching around
4.3 to 4.4 feet Friday and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 4.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 4.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.4 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

waterways.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Thursday to 4 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs
along tidal waterways. Some roads become impassable. Minor
damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most severe and impactful high tide
will be with Thursday morning's high tide, when major tidal
flooding is possible. Additional minor to moderate tidal
flooding is possible with Thursday night's high tide.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

too tight and watch out for overwash around boat ramps. Secure

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only

properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 5000 feet in elevation. Total snow
accumulations between 7 and 14 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40
mph.

* WHERE...Washington Pass.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult across Washington Pass.
Snowfall rates late Wednesday night into early Thursday morning
could approach one inch per hour at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures in the upper Methow Valley will
be near to just above freezing.  Heavier precipitation intensities
could drive wet snow down to valley floors at times near Mazama and
Winthrop with low confidence for accumulations.
properties.instruction:
For the latest travel information in Washington, go to
https://wsdot.wa.gov/travel

Persons should consider delaying travel or consider alternate routes.
If travel is absolutely necessary, drive with extreme caution.
Consider taking a winter storm kit along with you, including such
items as tire chains, booster cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets
and extra clothing. Also take water, a first aid kit, and anything
else that would help you survive in case you become stranded.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:50AM PST until November 26 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 945 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, +2.2
ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.7 ft MHHW
(6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, +2.1
ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.8 ft MHHW
(6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.4 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.3 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+6.9 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28 and +7.0 ft at 7:00 PM Sun
11/29.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Blowing Snow. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...No additional falling snow is expected. Strong
winds will blow snow already on the ground to create areas of low
visibility near the surface. A brief decrease in winds is expected
Wednesday before winds strengthen once more Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 11:28AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of North Carolina, including the following areas,
Alleghany NC, Ashe, Caswell, Rockingham, Stokes, Surry, Watauga,
Wilkes and Yadkin and Virginia, including the following areas,
Amherst, Appomattox, Bedford, Botetourt, Buckingham, Campbell,
Carroll, Charlotte, Floyd, Franklin, Grayson, Halifax, Henry,
Patrick, Pittsylvania, Roanoke and Rockbridge.

* WHEN...From 7 PM EST this evening through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several hours of moderate rainfall along and east of the Blue
Ridge mountains will lead to nuisance flooding in poor drainage
and leaf clogged drains through Thursday evening. Widespread
rainfall totals of 2 to 3 inches of rainfall are expected, with
localized totals up to 5 inches possible for favored upslope
locations along the Blue Ridge.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Freeze Warning issued November 25 at 9:28AM CST until November 26 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 31 expected.

* WHERE...Bell, Falls, Freestone, Limestone, McLennan, Anderson,
Leon, Milam, and Robertson Counties.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
properties.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (4.7 to 7.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...In Massachusetts, Southern Bristol MA and Southern
Plymouth MA Counties. In Rhode Island, Southeast Providence
RI, Eastern Kent RI, Bristol RI, Washington RI and Newport RI
Counties.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to 1 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding occurs along the most
vulnerable shoreline locales in Newport, Portsmouth and
Middletown. This includes flooding at parking lots near
beaches in Newport, and a portion of Hazard Road. Minor
coastal flooding also occurs on several streets in the Common
Fence Point area.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 2:55AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE THURSDAY NIGHT... ...COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM EST THURSDAY
